summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and a history of venous thromboses presented with hypotension following hemodialysis, during which she reportedly lost 7 kg of fluid. She experienced headache and visual spots but remained alert and mentating well. Initial blood pressure was 86/55 mmHg, which improved with intravenous fluids. Evaluation showed no evidence of sepsis, cardiogenic shock, or acute cardiac ischemia. Labs and chest imaging were unremarkable except for mild vascular congestion. Blood pressure variability suggested possible cuff inaccuracies, with leg measurements being more reliable. Chronic left arm and leg pain were evaluated with X-rays of the left hip and shoulder, which showed degenerative changes but no acute fractures. All home medications, including warfarin and insulin, were continued unchanged. The renal team coordinated with the dialysis center to limit future ultrafiltration to prevent recurrence. The patient stabilized and was discharged to extended care with instructions to monitor daily weight and follow up on musculoskeletal imaging.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
